$comment: NEW-59 (exponentialTalk (h)): THE work screen, the display coding agents drive with computer use, one spec ×4 (TS reference packages/domain-contract/src/work-screen.ts; desktop computer crate `work_screen` (the gate, the overlay rule) + ui device_settings (the row); iOS ExpCore WorkScreen.swift and Android domain/WorkScreen.kt mirror `copy` and `options` only). SETTING: per device, `launch_defaults.computerUseDisplay` = the 1-based NUMBER of the display in the device's own list (absent or null = Auto); same carry-forward as `computerUse` (a save without it keeps the stored one, an explicit null clears it to Auto). DISPLAYS: the device reports its displays in its doctor (`doctor.displays`, register + heartbeat): `[{number, width, height, primary}]` in the OS's order, pixels; absent = not reported (an older build, the CLI daemon without a display). UI: in device settings ×4 (web, the IDE, iOS, Android) the row `copy.row` is a picker row in the computer-use card, directly under the Computer use model row and only while computer use is on (the same group, the same picker row, no new component). Its options = `options(displays, stored)` (`optionCases`): `copy.auto` first, then one per reported display labelled `copy.display` with {number} plus ` · ` + `{width} × {height}`, plus ` · ` + `copy.primary` for the primary; a stored number the device no longer reports stays pickable at the end as `copy.display` + ` · ` + `copy.notConnected`. The row's value reads the picked option's label. GATE (desktop only; the `computer` hub enforces it, never the prompt; `gateCases`): `workDisplays(state)` = the 0-based indexes agents may drive: the picked display when it is connected, else (Auto, or the picked one is gone) every display WITHOUT a fullscreen app, in order. `state` = {count, picked (1-based number or null), fullscreen (0-based indexes holding a fullscreen window), active (0-based index of the focused window's display or null), activeFullscreen (the focused window is fullscreen)}. A display is a GAMING display when it holds a fullscreen app and is not a work display. `gate(state, call)` answers `allow` or the refusal `wrong_display` with one of `copy.refusals`: no work display at all = `noWorkScreen` for every tool but `wait`; `screenshot` with a `display` (0-based) outside the work displays = `notWorkScreen` ({number} = that display + 1, {work} = the work numbers joined with `, `); `activate_window` of a window whose centre lies on a non-work display = `windowElsewhere` (same fields, {number} = the window's display + 1); every INPUT tool (`left_click`, `right_click`, `middle_click`, `double_click`, `mouse_move`, `drag`, `scroll`, `type`, `key`, `activate_window`) while the focused window is fullscreen on a gaming display = `gaming` ({number} = that display + 1: the person is in it, and a foreground action would take their pointer and keyboard); `type` and `key` while the focused window sits on a non-work display = `keysElsewhere` (the keys would land there). Everything else is allowed; the run's current display is the picked `screenshot` display while it stays a work display, else the primary when it is one, else the first work display (`currentCases`). `list_windows` lists only windows whose centre lies on a work display and only the work displays (their indexes unchanged). A refusal is a tool result with isError true, the text `copy.refusals[kind]` and structuredContent {refusal: `wrong_display`, kind, work: [numbers]}. FULLSCREEN (per OS, read at every call): macOS = a layer-0 on-screen window of another app than the Dock/Finder/Window Server whose bounds equal a display's full bounds; Windows = a visible, non-tool top-level window (never Progman/WorkerW/the shell tray) whose rect covers its monitor's full rect; Linux X11 = a `_NET_CLIENT_LIST` window with `_NET_WM_STATE_FULLSCREEN`, on the display holding its centre. OVERLAY: the voice overlay (push to talk, the wake word, calls) never opens on a display with a fullscreen app: `overlayDisplay(state)` (`overlayCases`; state = {count, pointer (0-based display under the pointer), fullscreen, work}) = the pointer's display without one, else the first work display without one, else the first display without one, else null (the overlay stays hidden; the turn still runs and the reply is still spoken). BANNER: the computer-use banner (computer-use-banner.json) floats on the run's current display (the work screen), not the primary, with the session's label.

refusals.noWorkScreen: Every display has a fullscreen app, so there is no work screen right now. Wait, or ask the person to leave fullscreen.
refusals.notWorkScreen: Display {number} is not a work screen. Agents work on display {work}.
refusals.windowElsewhere: That window is on display {number}, not a work screen. Agents work on display {work}.
refusals.gaming: The person is in a fullscreen app on display {number}. Acting now would take their pointer and keyboard; wait until they leave it.
refusals.keysElsewhere: The focused window is on display {number}, not a work screen. Activate a window on display {work} first.

optionCases.name: a stored display that is gone stays pickable at the end

gateCases.name: Auto, nothing fullscreen: every display works, everything allowed
Auto, a game fullscreen on display 2 and focused: no input, display 2 refused
